speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly how long it has been since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Since the pain is shooting and triggered by eating or wearing earrings, are you currently experiencing any sensation of fluid draining from the ear or a feeling of fullness inside the canal?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (triggered by V3 nerve involvement or post-surgical changes).

The shooting pain triggered by eating (jaw movement) and the discomfort with earrings (touching the tragus) strongly suggest nerve irritation rather than an infection, especially given the history of chronic ear infections and recent surgery. Have you noticed any changes in the skin sensation on your cheek or forehead?
